pure-announcement.rationale: It is the OWASP project's reference page carrying the substance of the risk taxonomy itself, not a launch, release or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The supplied nearest concepts touch MCP governance and agentic visibility, but none contains the ten-category MCP risk taxonomy; a reader of remote-first-mcp-governance still learns the full attack-surface map here.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Each entry names concrete, independently documented attack classes (tool-poisoning sub-techniques, command injection, shadow servers) with a public GitHub repository as source.

durability.rationale: The ten risk classes — token mismanagement, scope creep, tool poisoning, supply chain, injection, intent subversion, authn/z gaps, missing audit, shadow servers, context over-sharing — are durable vulnerability categories even as the v0.1 beta's numbering and titles shuffle (MCP06 already appears under two different names on the page).

actionability.rationale: Like other OWASP Top 10s it works as a design-and-audit checklist, and entries carry concrete controls: short-lived scoped credentials, automated scope expiry, signed components with provenance tracking, immutable audit trails.

atomicity.rationale: The taxonomy is one stateable idea — the ten most critical MCP security risks — of which the entries are members, not unrelated bundled claims.
